external_evidence: uv's error shows the picked torchvision==0.27.1+df56172 from https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu has only win_arm64 wheels ("You're on Linux (manylinux_2_39_x86_64), but torchvision (v0.27.1+df56172) only has wheels for: win_arm64"). The defect is that the PyTorch CPU index serves a platform-specific Windows ARM build under a local label that sorts above the +cpu Linux build, so uv's universal lock (which resolves for all platforms) selects it. Package metadata lookup for that version returned HTTP 404, so this was not confirmed further.

rationale: The reporter's pyproject matches the documented PyTorch CPU-index configuration in docs/guides/integration/pytorch.md, so the config is valid and uv is not violating a documented contract. uv's lock is universal, so it resolves torchvision across all platforms and picks the highest version, which is the +df56172 local build whose only wheels are win_arm64; the install then fails on Linux. That points to the PyTorch index publishing a mis-labelled platform-specific build, which is outside uv. Possible uv-side mitigation is restricting the lock with [tool.uv] environments, or the reporter pinning torchvision to a +cpu version. No duplicate was found in search. Tool limits: the package metadata lookup returned HTTP 404 and no issue on the local-version ordering was found, so confidence is medium.
